title: H. Visual correctness and usability
definition: Nothing is clipped, nothing overlaps unintentionally, frames fit their contents, the layout is readable and navigable, key concepts stand out from supporting detail, and source evidence can be found.
questions: Are frames appropriately sized for their contents?
Is the layout readable and navigable?
Can users distinguish key concepts from supporting details?
Can users locate the source evidence when needed?

severity.critical: A link runs through a card (fatal layout issue); content clipped; a card outside its frame.
severity.major: Overlapping cards or frames; many link crossings.

deterministic: layout_no_fatal, layout_crossings_max (the product's layoutCheck on the rendered plan)
future: text clipping, measured in a browser (e2e) — not available in the offline suite
model_judge: Screenshot rubric 1–5: readability, emphasis on key ideas
human: By-hand look at the canvas at overview and 100% zoom

passCriteria: No fatal layout issue, no overlaps, every card inside its frame; screenshot score ≥ 4 on approved runs.
failCriteria: Any fatal layout issue or overlap.
passExample: Seven level frames side by side, each sized to its cards, arrows routed around cards, the main card in each frame larger.
failExample: An arrow cutting through the Reranker card; the L3 flow's last step sticking out of its frame.

judgeScale.meaning: Readable with effort; a few crossings or cramped frames.
Clean, navigable, the main ideas stand out, evidence one click away.
